issues.description: The problem statement describes correct_teleportation(teleportation_measurements, x_measurements) where the first argument is the teleportation measurement results and the second is the X-basis measurements. In the solution, calls to correct_teleportation pass the final (X-basis) measurements as the first argument and the teleportation measurements as the second argument (e.g. correct_teleportation(measurements[:, final], measurements[:, tele])). This mismatch between the documented parameter order and the actual call sites is inconsistent and likely to confuse students reading the API and the solution. Even though XOR is symmetric (so the specific implementation here happens to be order-insensitive), the ordering in the docs, function signature, and usage should be consistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ordering explicit and consistent: either (A) update all calls to correct_teleportation to pass teleportation measurements first and X-basis measurements second (e.g. correct_teleportation(measurements[:, tele], measurements[:, final])), or (B) change the function documentation/signature to reflect the order used at call sites. Ensure the docstring, function definition, and all call sites agree so students are not confused about which measurement array corresponds to which parameter.
